# Results — Study 959 (Crypto Fee War) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The ten US spot-bitcoin ETFs
that were approved together and began trading on the **same day, 2024-01-11**, measured
against **BTC-USD** (24/7 spot) and against each other. A wrapper's **tracking difference**
(TD) is what it delivered minus what the asset delivered, in basis points per year; for
these funds the only recurring contractual leak is the sponsor fee, so a clean tape should
hand the fee back. Three estimators (endpoint, HAC trend slope, non-overlapping monthly
mean); the headline is always the monthly one. The headline **spread** is fund-minus-fund
and uses **no fee input at all**. Exactly one execution lag, and only where something
trades: the quarterly tracking-winner rotation ranks on data through the last session of a
quarter and switches at the **next** session's close, paying a full round trip — sell plus
buy, 2 × 2 bp × NAV — on every change of fund. No short
leg in the ownership race; the long/short version pays borrow, swept. Daily closes
(`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`). As-of **2026-06-30** — the partial current month is
dropped so the monthly estimator never eats a stub.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Complete months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| IBIT, FBTC, ARKB, BITB, HODL, BRRR, BTCO, EZBC, BTCW, GBTC + BTC-USD | 2024-01-11 → 2026-06-30 | 618 | 29 | `8463d167f5aa` |

Cross-checks cached alongside: **BTC** (Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust, 15 bp, launched
2024-07-31 — out of cohort) and **BIL** (the cash leg for the excess-of-cash race).
**DEFI** (Hashdex) is excluded by name in `data.EXCLUDED`: it was a bitcoin *futures* fund
until its 2024-03-27 spot conversion, so its first quarter is not a spot wrapper and it
cannot share the cohort's common window.

**Price-only vs total-return.** `auto_adjust=True` gives distribution-adjusted closes, but
**none of these wrappers has ever paid a distribution**, so for them adjusted = price and
the two labels coincide. **BTC-USD is a price-only spot quote** — bitcoin pays no coupon,
and none of these US wrappers stakes or lends its coin, so a price benchmark is the correct
one here (unlike Study 913, where a price-only index proxy silently prints the dividend
yield as a "tracking difference"). **BIL is genuine total return** and is used only for the
excess-of-cash Sharpe race.

**Survivorship: named, and small.** The cohort is the *entire* January-2024 batch, alive
from day one to as-of — nothing has been closed, merged or de-listed, so there is no
survivor filter on the Signal axis. What there *is* instead is **hindsight in the fee
sheet** (below) and a **29-month sample**: this is the newest wrapper race on the desk, and
its whole history is one bitcoin cycle.

**Non-tape inputs (ASSUMPTIONS, all swept).**
(i) **The fee schedule** — IBIT 25, FBTC 25, ARKB 21, BITB 20, HODL 20, BRRR 25, BTCO 25,
EZBC 19, BTCW 25, GBTC **150** bp/yr, as published at build time. Not measured, and it
carries whatever hindsight the current sheet carries. It enters **only** the fee-rank test;
the headline spread is pure tape. The rank test is therefore run three ways: against the
headline sheet, against the waiver-blended sheet, and with GBTC dropped.
(ii) **The waiver schedule** — launch fee waivers and their *scheduled* end dates. Several
were capped by an AUM threshold the tape cannot see (IBIT's 12 bp introductory rate was
capped at the first $5bn, crossed within weeks), so the stated end date may overstate how
long the waiver actually ran.
(iii) **The borrow rate** on the short leg, and (iv) **the tax rate and embedded gain** in
the switch break-even. Both swept rather than picked.

## The measurement floor — why the instrument is fund-versus-fund

| Difference measured | Daily sd | Smallest \|*t*\|=2-detectable gap on 29 months |
|---|--:|--:|
| a fund minus **BTC-USD** | **134.7 bp** | **481 bp/yr** |
| a fund minus **another wrapper** | **8.9 bp** | **66 bp/yr** |

Bitcoin trades 24/7; the ETFs are struck at 16:00 New York. Every fund-versus-spot
comparison therefore carries a mean-zero **clock stub** worth ~135 bp *per day*, and a
20 bp/yr fee is 0.08 bp/day. Against a sibling wrapper the stub is common and cancels, and
the same difference collapses by **15.2×**. This single ratio decides the whole study: the
fund-versus-fund spread is the instrument, and the fund-versus-spot number is an
indication, never a test.

|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| IBIT | 25 | −41.3 | −25.0 (−5.16) | −15.7 (−0.13) | +5.1 (+0.38) |
| FBTC | 25 | −45.6 | −20.5 (−4.28) | −13.1 (−0.12) | +7.8 (+1.04) |
| ARKB | 21 | −46.5 | −20.8 (−4.37) | −9.5 (−0.08) | +11.4 (+1.10) |
| BITB | 20 | −49.9 | −18.0 (−3.70) | −9.3 (−0.09) | +11.6 (+1.88) |
| HODL | 20 | −23.9 | +0.2 (+0.05) | +12.3 (+0.11) | +33.2 (+4.10) |
| BRRR | 25 | −56.9 | −21.1 (−4.40) | −8.7 (−0.08) | +12.2 (+1.63) |
| BTCO | 25 | −25.1 | −19.4 (−4.12) | −2.2 (−0.02) | +18.7 (+1.29) |
| EZBC | 19 | −29.9 | −15.5 (−3.33) | −3.6 (−0.03) | +17.3 (+1.66) |
| BTCW | 25 | −19.1 | −17.2 (−3.62) | −9.6 (−0.09) | +11.3 (+0.74) |
| **GBTC** | **150** | **−79.4** | **−156.8 (−33.22)** | **−149.4 (−1.39)** | **−128.5 (−9.57)** |

Read the columns against the floor, not against each other. The **monthly vs BTC** column
is *worthless* — GBTC's −149.4 bp/yr, the one number in it that is unambiguously true,
carries a *t* of −1.39, because 481 bp/yr is the smallest gap that column can resolve. The
**trend slope** column is much sharper (618 anchors, not 2) but its residual is a persistent
premium/discount, so its HAC *t* is optimistic and it is quoted, never leaned on. The
**cohort-relative monthly** column is the honest one: the clock stub is gone, GBTC prints
−128.5 bp/yr at *t* = −9.57, and no other fund is distinguishable from the pack — except
HODL at +33.2 (*t* = +4.10), which is discussed below.

The **endpoint** estimator is the trap the desk expects a fee-war blog post to fall into: it
puts GBTC at −79.4 bp/yr, roughly *half* its true leak, because 2024-01-11 was GBTC's
conversion day and its closing discount that afternoon flatters every subsequent comparison
to it. One estimator, two anchors, an answer that is wrong by 70 bp/yr.

## The headline — cheapest minus priciest (pure tape, no fee input)

**EZBC − GBTC: +145.8 bp/yr, HAC *t* = +8.43**, positive in **26 of 29** months.
Block-bootstrap 95% CI **[+110.5, +187.0] bp/yr**, share of resamples below zero **0.0000**.
Monthly sd 12.4 bp, daily sd 10.2 bp.

Every cheap wrapper against GBTC tells the same story:

| Fund − GBTC | bp/yr | HAC *t* | months positive |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| IBIT | +133.6 | +7.04 | 24/29 |
| FBTC | +136.3 | +8.23 | 25/29 |
| ARKB | +139.9 | +7.31 | 25/29 |
| BITB | +140.1 | +9.77 | 27/29 |
| HODL | +161.7 | +10.56 | 28/29 |
| BRRR | +140.7 | +9.36 | 26/29 |
| BTCO | +147.2 | +5.80 | 24/29 |
| EZBC | +145.8 | +8.43 | 26/29 |
| BTCW | +139.8 | +6.76 | 24/29 |

Nine independent wrappers, nine *t*-statistics between +5.8 and +10.6, all in the direction
the fee sheet predicts, and all clustered on the **130 bp** gap between 150 and ~20. The
fee is not approximately delivered; it is delivered.

### Is the headline an artefact of its own two anchors?

**It has two anchors, and the study says so.** Log increments telescope, so the mean of
non-overlapping monthly tracking differences is *algebraically identical* to an endpoint
estimate taken between the first and last complete month-end (2024-01-31 and 2026-06-30).
It is not anchor-free; what it buys over the raw endpoint estimator is a pair of anchors
that excludes GBTC's contaminated 2024-01-11 conversion close, plus a dispersion the
endpoint estimator cannot give at all. The anchors are therefore tested directly:

| Check | Estimate | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| headline (29 months, both anchors) | **+145.8** | +8.43 |
| trim 1 month off **both** ends (27) | +141.7 | +7.78 |
| trim 2 months off both ends (25) | +140.5 | +7.18 |
| trim 3 months off both ends (23) | +135.6 | +6.06 |
| OLS trend slope, **all 618 sessions as anchors** | +141.3 | (HAC optimistic: resid acf1 0.80) |
| same slope, median of the nine cheap legs | +140.1 | — |

Every anchor-free version of the question returns **135–142 bp/yr**. The headline is ~5 bp
rich against them — the first months carry the tail of GBTC's discount closing, which is
the same thing the era cut shows — and nothing here depends on the choice of endpoint. The
honest number to carry away is *about 140 bp/yr*, not 145.8 to one decimal.

## Era cut (split 2025-01-01)

| Era | months | EZBC − GBTC | HAC *t* | months positive |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2024 | 11 | **+186.5 bp/yr** | +5.76 | 9/11 |
| 2025–2026 | 18 | **+120.9 bp/yr** | +9.10 | 17/18 |

Positive and significant in **both** halves. The early era runs hot — 2024 is when GBTC's
discount was still closing and the outflow was heaviest — and the late era, at +120.9
bp/yr, is the cleaner estimate of the steady-state leak. It is also the era with the tighter
*t*: as the discount noise faded, the fee showed through more clearly, not less.

## Does the fee *ranking* predict the tracking-difference ranking?

Spearman(fee, cohort-relative TD) against an exact/sampled permutation null. A working fee
ladder implies a **negative** rank correlation. Waiver-blended effective fees (an
ASSUMPTION): IBIT 19.7, FBTC 19.4, ARKB 16.8, BITB 16.0, HODL 10.1, BRRR 22.5, BTCO 20.0,
EZBC 14.7, BTCW 20.0, GBTC 150.0.

| Fee sheet | Universe | Spearman | perm *p* | needs \|ρ\| > | pass-through TD = a + b·fee | R² |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|
| headline | all ten | **−0.642** | 0.0514 | 0.642 | −1.124 | 0.978 |
| headline | cheap nine (ex-GBTC) | −0.495 | 0.179 | 0.688 | −1.522 | 0.247 |
| waiver-blended | all ten | −0.498 | 0.147 | 0.644 | −1.083 | 0.985 |
| waiver-blended | cheap nine | −0.310 | 0.408 | 0.678 | −1.645 | 0.552 |

Two things are true at once, and the study refuses to collapse them.

- **The pass-through lands near −1 — on one anchor.** Regress the cohort-relative TD on the
  published fee across all ten funds and the slope is **−1.12** (waiver-blended **−1.08**)
  with **R² = 0.98**. A wrapper that leaks its fee and nothing else gives −1.00. But that
  R² is **one point doing all the work**: the cross-section is nine funds inside a 6 bp band
  plus GBTC 125 bp away. Drop GBTC and the slope becomes an unstable **−1.52 with R² =
  0.25**. The right reading is not "the fee sheet explains 98% of the cross-section" — it is
  "the *one* fee difference big enough to see is delivered at roughly one-for-one, and the
  regression is measuring that single fact."
- **The *rank* test does not clear — it lands exactly on the ceiling.** ρ = −0.642 is the
  *largest* rank correlation this fee vector can attain, and it is also, to three decimals,
  the permutation null's own 5% critical value (*p* = 0.0514). A sheet with five funds tied
  at 25 bp cannot generate a finer statistic, so the rank test on ten funds is not a test
  that failed — it is a test with no room to succeed. Drop GBTC and the rank
  correlation among the cheap nine is **not significant on any sheet** (*p* = 0.18 to 0.41),
  and R² falls to 0.25.

That is not a contradiction; it is the floor again. Inside the cheap tier the entire fee
spread is **6 bp/yr** (19 to 25) and the smallest gap 29 months can resolve is **66 bp/yr** —
eleven times larger. The cross-section carries one resolvable fee fact, GBTC's, and the
regression finds it; the rank statistic asks a finer question than the tape can answer.

**HODL, the exception that names the limit.** VanEck's wrapper prints +33.2 bp/yr against
the cohort at *t* = +4.10 — the only cheap fund distinguishable from the pack, and it beats
the cohort by more than its own 20 bp fee. A fund cannot out-earn the coin it holds by
holding it; the residual is a quoting artefact (its 16:00 print sits systematically on the
other side of the pack's) plus the longest waiver in the cohort, scheduled to 2025-03-31.
The desk names it rather than promoting it to a finding.

## Do the waiver expiries show up in the tape?

Step in each fund's cohort-relative monthly TD at its scheduled waiver end. A waiver that
expires should print a **negative** step of roughly the headline fee.

| Fund | Waiver end | Pre | Post | Step | Welch *t* | Expected step |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| IBIT | 2025-01-10 | −20.9 | +21.1 | **+42.0** | +0.73 | −13 |
| FBTC | 2024-07-31 | +18.3 | +5.0 | −13.3 | −0.30 | −25 |
| ARKB | 2024-07-11 | +34.6 | +6.6 | −28.0 | −0.22 | −21 |
| BITB | 2024-07-11 | +4.0 | +13.2 | **+9.2** | +0.18 | −20 |
| HODL | 2025-03-31 | +28.9 | +37.2 | **+8.3** | +0.25 | −20 |
| BTCO | 2024-07-11 | −23.8 | +27.5 | **+51.2** | +0.47 | −25 |
| EZBC | 2024-08-02 | +26.1 | +15.0 | −11.1 | −0.11 | −19 |
| BTCW | 2024-07-11 | +19.0 | +9.6 | −9.3 | −0.17 | −25 |

**No.** Not one step clears \|*t*\| = 0.8, and **four of the eight have the wrong sign**.
BRRR and GBTC have too few months on one side to test at all. This is exactly what the floor
predicts: a 20 bp/yr waiver expiry is a **1.7 bp step in a monthly series whose sd is 12 bp**,
observed with six to twelve months on each side. The event study is not evidence that the
waivers were fictional — it is a demonstration that a public daily tape cannot see them.
The scheduled dates are themselves an ASSUMPTION (several waivers were AUM-capped and
ended early), which can only make the test weaker.

## Cross-check — Grayscale's own Mini Trust (BTC, 15 bp, out of cohort)

| Pair | months from 2024-07-31 | bp/yr | HAC *t* | months positive |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| BTC − GBTC | 23 | **+130.6** | +2.84 | 20/23 |
| BTC − EZBC | 23 | **−0.0** | −0.00 | 10/23 |

The strongest possible control: *the same sponsor, the same coin, the same custodian, the
same 16:00 strike* — differing only in the fee, 15 bp against 150. The gap is +130.6 bp/yr,
almost exactly the 135 bp fee difference. And measured against a cheap third-party wrapper,
Grayscale's Mini Trust is indistinguishable from zero. The 130 bp is the fee, not Grayscale.

## The ownership race, excess-of-cash (2 bp one-way, one execution lag)

617 common days with BIL. Rotation: rank on trailing three-month cohort-relative TD at each
quarter end, switch at the next session's close, 7 switches over the window.

| Arm | Excess Sharpe | CAGR | Vol | Total return |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| own_cheapest (EZBC) | **+0.3467** | +9.67% | 49.9% | +25.36% |
| own_priciest (GBTC) | +0.3365 | +9.13% | 49.9% | +23.84% |
| rotate_winner | +0.3457 | +9.64% | 49.8% | +25.28% |

**Sharpe gap, cheapest − priciest: +0.0102.** The most decisive fee fact on the desk is a
rounding error in a Sharpe ratio, because the asset carries **50% annualised volatility** and
the fee is 1.2 bp a month. Chasing last quarter's tracking winner earns *less* than simply
owning the cheapest fund and never trading (+25.28% vs +25.36%) — the rotation pays 7
switches to end up where doing nothing already was.

## Acting on it — what the 140 bp is actually worth

**(1) A new purchase, or a switch inside a tax-shelter.** At the +145.8 bp/yr headline
spread a round-trip switch out of GBTC repays itself in:

| One-way cost | Days to repay |
|---|--:|
| 0 bp | 0.0 |
| 2 bp | 10.0 |
| 5 bp | 25.0 |
| 10 bp | 50.1 |
| 25 bp | 125.2 |

Even at a punitive 25 bp one-way, the switch is repaid inside five months and free forever
after. This is the one unambiguously bankable action in the study — and it is a **purchase
decision, not a strategy**.

**(2) A taxable switch** (tax rate and embedded gain are ASSUMPTIONS, swept). Selling a
holding with embedded gain *g* realises *g*/(1+*g*) of current NAV as gain:

| Tax rate | Embedded gain | Cost today | Years to repay |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 15% | +50% | 5.00% | 3.5 |
| 20% | +100% | 10.00% | 7.2 |
| 20% | +300% | 15.00% | 11.1 |
| 23.8% | +300% | 17.85% | 13.5 |

A GBTC holder from 2020 sitting on a 300% gain needs **eleven to fourteen years** of the fee
spread to repay the tax bill. The right answer for them is *not* to switch, which is
precisely why Grayscale can still charge 150 bp in a market where the going rate is 20.

**(3) The market-neutral version** — long the cheap wrapper, short GBTC. Self-financing, so
the spread is already an excess return; but **the short pays borrow** (an ASSUMPTION, swept),
and a hard-to-borrow legacy trust in permanent outflow is exactly where borrow is dear.
Costs: a round trip on **each** of the two legs, once a year — four one-way crossings at
2 bp = **8 bp/yr**, already deducted below (145.8 gross → 137.8 before borrow).

| Borrow | Net | |
|---|--:|---|
| 0 bp/yr | +137.8 | alive |
| 25 | +112.8 | alive |
| 50 | +87.8 | alive |
| 100 | +37.8 | alive |
| **150** | **−12.2** | **dead** |
| 200 | −62.2 | dead |
| 300 | −162.2 | dead |

The trade survives to roughly **135 bp/yr of borrow** and dies above it. GBTC borrow has not
been in that neighbourhood for the whole window — but the desk does not own the borrow tape,
so the honest statement is: *this is a 140 bp gross spread on a 50%-vol pair, and whether it
nets anything is decided entirely by a number this study cannot observe.*

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

| World | Pair spread (planted) | Pair *t* | Spearman (*p*) | Pass-through slope | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| planted fee ladder | +124.4 (131) | +6.55 | −0.545 (0.121) | **−0.970** | 0.995 |
| null: one fee, dispersed sheet | −7.9 (0) | −0.44 | +0.487 (0.165) | +0.039 | 0.243 |

The size-and-power sweep below is reproduced by `python examples/verify.py --sweep`
(offline, fixed seeds, a few minutes).

**Null size, 120 seeds:** mean Spearman **+0.016**, the rank test fires at 5% on **4.2%** of
seeds (correctly sized), and the pair instrument's \|*t*\| **never once exceeds 2** (max
0.92). **Power, 24 seeds:** the pair spread recovers the planted gap with a mean *t* of
**+7.00** and the pass-through slope lands at **−1.010 ± 0.045**, R² 0.986 — while the rank
test fires on only **9/24**. The harness reproduces, on a planted world, exactly the split
the real tape shows: **the pair spread and the pass-through regression see a fee; the rank
statistic, given a sheet with five funds tied at one number, mostly does not.** That is a
property of rank statistics on a tied fee sheet, not a defect of either tape.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Real.** The headline is a fund-versus-fund monthly spread that uses **no fee
  input whatsoever** — the pair is named by the published fee sheet before any outcome is
  looked at, and the cheap leg chosen that way (EZBC) is *not* the widest of the nine
  (HODL is), so the choice does not flatter the result. It prints **+145.8 bp/yr with HAC
  *t* = +8.43**, bootstrap CI [+110.5, +187.0] entirely above zero, positive in 26 of 29
  months, positive and significant in **both** eras, replicated across **nine** independent
  cheap wrappers (*t* = +5.8 to +10.6), and it survives its own anchors: trimming months off
  both ends and re-estimating with all 618 sessions as anchors both return **135–142 bp/yr**.
  The cleanest control the desk has ever had — Grayscale's *own* 15 bp Mini Trust against
  its 150 bp flagship, same sponsor, same coin, same custodian — hands back **+130.6 bp/yr**
  against a 135 bp fee difference. The tape delivers the fee, at about **140 bp/yr**.
- **What is *not* real.** The *fine-grained* fee ranking. Inside the cheap tier the whole fee
  spread is 6 bp/yr against a 66 bp/yr detection floor; the rank correlation among the nine
  cheap funds is insignificant on every fee sheet (*p* = 0.18–0.41), and the all-ten rank
  test lands *on* its own attainable ceiling without clearing 5% (*p* = 0.0514, and only
  because GBTC is in it at all). The waiver
  expiries are **invisible**: no step clears \|*t*\| = 0.8 and half have the wrong sign.
  Anyone ranking IBIT against FBTC on realised tracking is reading noise.
- **Tradability — Fragile.** The 140 bp is real and it is also **not a strategy**. In the
  ownership race it is worth **+0.010 of Sharpe** — invisible against 50% volatility. The
  rotation rule under-performs doing nothing. The long/short is a 140 bp gross spread whose
  survival is decided by a **borrow rate this study cannot observe** (dead above ~135 bp/yr,
  on a name that is permanently hard to borrow). And for the holder who actually owns the
  expensive fund — a GBTC investor with a large embedded gain — switching takes **7 to 14
  years** to repay the tax. What is bankable here is a *purchase* decision: if you are buying
  today, buy a 20 bp wrapper, never trade it, and collect ~135 bp/yr for the rest of the
  holding period. That is worth having and it is not an edge.
- **Sample.** 29 months, one bitcoin cycle, one wrapper cohort. The fee arithmetic will not
  change; everything else here should be re-read in five years.
